soundcheck.heard: A Kodiak woman asked Google when Snipe Season opens. It's AI answer said September 1st, so on September 5th she shot three Snipe. At home she looked up the state regulations and saw her mistake. She called troopers and turned herself in. The Troopers report says the general season opened October 8th. So two pages disagreed, which one can a hunter trust? That trooper ran her exact search. He got the same wrong answer. She still pleaded no contest and paid $150. She told the Alaska beacon, I feel terrible. State spokesman Austin McDaniel thinks it's the first time AI has been cited. He expects more. And their warnings, their work. Google's help page says AI answers may include mistakes and to check more than one place. Google didn't respond to the beacon's request for comment. McDaniel says the one source of truth is Fish and Games regulations and emergency orders. But that source has a catch. Fish and Games own page says its online regulations are simplified and emergency orders can override them. So even the official page is a summary. The answer was on top. What counts sits underneath. Check the regulations and any emergency order. Fish and Game will mail you a copy. Before you hunt, what do you check?
